stories.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video clips
paragraphs: On Nov. 5, 2026, Google said Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is generally available on the Gemini API and Google Cloud. Product manager Anish Nangia wrote that the update adds native video up to 15 seconds (up from 10 seconds on Omni 1.1), multi-turn conversational editing, stronger reference following, and a 30% price cut to $0.07 per second for 720p video.

According to the Google DeepMind post, creators can draft at 360p or 720p, fix details with follow-up edits instead of regenerating whole clips, then upscale selected results to 1080p or 4K. Duration can be set in one-second steps from 3 to 15 seconds.

Google says the model holds character, product, and style references—including faces, garments, packaging type, and brand colors—more consistently across camera moves, and supports short motion clips up to three seconds plus audio cues. Multi-turn edits can swap backgrounds, lighting, weather, or aspect ratio without restarting from scratch.

The company also cites more natural multi-speaker dialogue and lip-sync, steadier cinematic camera moves with fewer jump cuts, and an imperceptible SynthID watermark on outputs. Provisioned Throughput is available for enterprise use on Google Cloud.

stories.title: OpenAI introduces Images 2.6 with Flare, Sunburst, GIFs, and SVG export
paragraphs: MarkTechPost reports that OpenAI shipped Images 2.6 on Nov. 4, 2026, across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, saying generation is 50% faster than before and that users now create more than 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and the API.

According to MarkTechPost's summary of the launch, the API adds GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for fast iteration—returning images in as little as six seconds at low quality—and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst for higher detail and stronger edit consistency. ChatGPT users can create animated GIFs, edit frames, and save reusable reference images.

MarkTechPost also lists markup-guided edits, SVG export, GIF output, and a complexity parameter (low, medium, or high; default high) separate from quality, with token pricing matching the prior image release.

stories.title: Together AI's Compiler uses agents to re-optimize inference as traffic changes
paragraphs: Together AI said on Nov. 4, 2026, that Together Compiler (TKCC) is a continual compilation loop in which coding agents rewrite a model's forward pass while a persistent serving engine hot-reloads candidates instead of restarting for every trial. The company says the system already runs on several of its serverless endpoints.

According to Together's research post, the loop takes a launch command, traffic profile, and hardware config, then measures candidates with fast few-layer and slower many-layer engine tiers. Together reports up to 2.6× higher tokens per second than the best published InferenceX configurations in under 24 hours per setting, and about 252× higher experiment throughput than an engine-restart baseline.

MarkTechPost notes self-reported batch-size-1 gains such as 1,111 versus 633 P90 TPS per user on MiniMax M3.1 Flash on NVIDIA B200 hardware, with smaller gains on some AMD MI355X runs. Together says agents work across NVIDIA B200/B300/GB300/H100, AMD MI355X, and AWS Trainium2.

stories.title: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base as a 280B MoE pre-training checkpoint
paragraphs: Baidu said on Nov. 5, 2026, that ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base is a sparse mixture-of-experts text model with 280 billion total parameters and 14 billion activated per token. The released weights stop at the end of pre-training, with no mid- or post-training, as a baseline for fine-tuning and research.

According to Baidu, the model was pre-trained on 33.5 trillion tokens with a 128K training context and up to 1M tokens for fine-tuning and inference. Architecture highlights include hybrid Heavily Compressed Attention and Multi-head Latent Attention layers, Multi-Router Latent MoE with 512 routed experts (top-10) plus one shared expert, and an ECHO multi-token prediction head.

MarkTechPost notes Baidu's unified-pipeline scores of 78.4 on MMLU-Pro and 82.3 on HumanEval+, with FP8 and BF16 weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope under the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base Model License Agreement v1.0. Benchmark figures are self-reported by Baidu.
